标题: 浓烟半分钟上蹿百米 ！ 高层建筑失火为何难扑灭 ？
正文2000: 11月26日，香港大埔多栋住宅楼发生重大火灾事故，致数十人遇难。至次日晚，灭火救援工作仍在继续。为何高层建筑起火难以扑灭？如何科学自救？ 高楼起火为何蔓延快，扑救难？ 据香港消防处披露，香港大埔宏福苑于26日14时51分发生火警，15时34分火警升为四级，并于18时22分升为五级——仅次于最高等级“灾难级”。至27日晚，消防处的灭火救援工作仍然持续进行。 据悉，该楼群落成于1983年，共有8座楼宇，每座31层。火灾蔓延至7座大厦，仅剩一座大厦未被波及。 11月26日拍摄的火灾救援现场。新华社记者 陈铎 摄 为何火势发展如此迅猛？与普通建筑相比，高层建筑“立体燃烧”的复杂性更为突出。 首先，“烟囱效应”会使火势迅速蔓延。 “烟囱效应”是指户内空气沿着垂直坡度的空间向上升或下降，造成空气加强对流的现象。在高层建筑内部，楼梯间、管道井等各种竖向管井构造如同烟囱。火灾发生时，易形成气流对流，使得烟气和火焰迅速蔓延。 建筑高度越高，烟囱效应越明显。在火灾发展阶段，高层建筑中的烟火垂直蔓延速度平均为每秒3～4米，在超高层建筑（100米以上）中甚至可以达到每秒8米。也就是说，浓烟从一座30层、高约100米的建筑一楼蔓延至顶楼仅需30秒。 其次，高处风力大，使火势更难以控制。 建筑高度大于27m的住宅，大于24m的非单层厂房仓库和其他民用建筑，都属于高层建筑。据测定，高层建筑30米处风速8.7米/秒，60米处风速12.3米/秒，90米处风速可达到15米/秒。楼层越高，风速越大，火灾发生后往往会出现风助火势、火借风威，越烧越旺的态势。 此外，易燃可燃外保温材料也是重要“帮凶”。 我国从2005年开始推行建筑节能政策，主要措施之一就是在外墙增加保温层，由于以前对外墙保温材料危险性认识不足，对材料的燃烧性能并无明确规定，当时多采用聚苯乙烯泡沫板或聚氨酯硬质泡沫等易燃可燃材料，这些材料极易引燃且蔓延迅速，燃烧后产生大量有毒烟气，火灾危险性很大。 此次香港大埔火灾事故中，香港警方调查发现，建筑物外墙有保护网、防水帆布、塑料布，疑未符合防火标准，另有一座未波及的大厦每层电梯大堂窗外都有发泡胶包封，易燃且可能加速火势蔓延，不排除发泡胶是火势迅速蔓延的原因。 遭遇火情，“跑”还是“等”？ 高层建筑发生火灾时，是立即逃生，还是等待救援？ 发生火灾时，最好能判断火源点，再判断先灭火还是逃生。在火源确定且火势可控状态时，切忌惊慌失措，应利用周围的灭火器、消火栓等消防设施器材协助扑救初起火灾。 如无法扑灭，需要根据火势和烟雾情况来应对，做到“小火快跑、浓烟关门”。 🔸 “小火快跑”： 开门前先触摸门把手，若温度不高，且门缝无烟气渗入，再开门。如果火势没有挡住逃生路线，疏散楼梯间无明显烟气，应尽快逃生。 逃生时用浸湿的毛巾或衣物捂好口鼻，减少烟气对呼吸道的侵害；弯腰低姿态前行，避开上方浓烟；不要乘坐电梯，穿越常闭式防火门时应随手关门。 🔸 “浓烟关门”： 如果入户门把手发热，门底缝隙有烟气渗入，说明大火或浓烟已封锁房门出口，千万别贸然打开房门；如果门把手不热，开门发现走廊里没有烟，但楼梯间里有烟，也应立即退回室内。这种情况下，不要盲目开门逃生，因为几口有毒的浓烟就会让人昏厥，进而窒息身亡。 应立即关上房门，用湿毛巾封堵门缝，减少烟气进入，拨打119告知自己被困房间的位置，等待救援。同时不断用水淋湿入户门，防止外部高温烘烤，火势蔓延。在靠近窗口的位置通过打手电筒、挥舞衣物等方式发出求救信号。 逃生时，向上跑还是向下跑？ 遭遇高层建筑起火，符合“小火快跑”的撤离条件时，应该向上跑还是向下跑呢？ 这需要从起火楼层与自己的相对位置、具体火情来判断： 🔸火势可控且逃生通道畅通时，优先往下跑。 火灾发生在上方楼层，从容向下撤离，记得关闭窗户，防止火星进入；火灾来自同一楼层或下方，且疏散楼梯间无明显烟气，应尽快向下跑。 在疏散逃生时，要熟悉了解所居住场所的疏散通道和安全出口位置情况，一般高层建筑都有至少两部以上的楼梯可供疏散，着火时切勿使用电梯。 🔸 遇特殊情况迫不得已时，再考虑往上跑。 专家一般不建议向上跑，一是很难跑过烟气蔓延；二是逃离过程中被烟熏，有中毒危险，不如在家用湿毛巾把门缝堵实。 但遭遇极端情况，比如火灾发生在下方楼层，但向下逃生通道被封堵，无法安全撤离，且所在房间已无法停留、必须转移时，可以考虑向上跑，尽量跑到便于消防登高车触及的窗口，选择相对安全的楼层暂时躲避，或通过天台进入相邻单元逃生。 此次香港大埔火灾事故中，消防员于27日11时在一座大厦的31楼成功救出一名男性长者，为其戴上呼吸器后带至天台，成功由天台救到地面并将其送院进行救治。 此外，对于超高层建筑，在逃生受阻情况下，人员可就近疏散到避难层——相关规定要求，建筑高度大于100米的住宅或公共建筑必须设置消防

标题: 汕头自建房火灾始末|楼房|陈辉|铺面|五金店|汕头市
正文2000: 事发五金店。澎湃新闻记者 陈灿杰 图 这是一栋典型的潮汕地区“三合一”自建房，一楼开五金店，二楼作仓储，三楼住着奶奶和父母，四楼住着兄弟三家人。 几十年间，临街铺面从三间扩容成五间，看着蒸蒸日上。 直到一场大火毁了所有。三代人经营的五金店没了，四代同堂的家族中，12人丧生。 12月9日晚，位于广东汕头潮南区峡山街道的这栋四层自建房发生重大火灾，潮南区消防救援大队发布警情通报称，过火面积约150平方米。 火灾发生后，澎湃记者实地走访发现，事发地所在的峡山街道丹凤路上，多为类似的“三合一”式建筑，即经营、仓库、住宿混合，多处一楼店铺闭门停业。 仍在营业的数家商铺经营者均提到，今年以来已接受多次消防检查，沿街店铺需配有喷淋、烟感、灭火器等消防设施，否则停电停水。然而，一名知情人士称，事发五金店此前已办理消防合格证，但更多可能是应付日常检查，“除了喷淋没水，烟感也不正常”。 12月10日上午，广东省政府召开全省安全生产和消防工作视频会议，要求深刻汲取汕头“12·9”自建房重大火灾教训，对立即开展重大火灾风险隐患排查整治行动进行动员部署。近日，澎湃新闻在当地看到，当地已有建筑在安装防火门，以将楼下经营场所与楼上区隔。 中冶建筑研究总院（深圳）有限公司正高级工程师闵红光博士向澎湃新闻表示，“三合一”自建房是火灾高风险区，因可燃物多，没有严格的防火分隔，缺乏必要的消防设施设备，“一旦起火，极易导致群死群伤”。他建议，应建立房屋安全档案并信息化管理，建立跨部门综合监管体系，对自建房进行每年不少于一次的定期检查。 “主要就是那个烟在冲上去” 邻居陈辉说，发生火灾的五金店一般开到晚上近11点，常能看到店主和儿子在店里喝茶，事发当天，他们恰好关门较早。 这家店名为裕丰五金电器店，吴先生是店主的大儿子，起火时不在家。当晚9点22分，他接到妻子电话，得知家中失火，随后紧忙报警并驱车回家。 他赶到店里时，是9点28分，妻子两臂拽着两个小孩从店后门跑出，十岁的大女儿则已经打开正门逃生，“头发还被火烧焦了”，大女儿“应该是被黑烟熏到眼睛，看不见，没有方向感，就往前面冲”。吴先生说自己两次尝试进入正门，都被浓烟呛了出来。他的另外三个孩子和其他亲人还在着火的房子里。 当时，住在五金店对门的林斌和街坊一起，从紧邻厂房的消防栓接消防水带灭火，但很快发现是杯水车薪，“主要就是那个烟在冲上去”。现场视频显示，透过该店临街一侧关着的木头正门，能看到店内有剧烈火光，浓烟滚滚。伴随店内响彻街头的燃爆声，火势瞬间冲出门缝。 据相关道路监控信息，9点24分前后，距五金店约4.6公里的峡山消防救援站出动了两辆消防车；9点32分，距五金店约2.2公里的峡山管区消防义务队出动了一辆消防车。另据多名参与救火的街坊回忆，报警后共有6辆消防车陆续抵达，除上述两支消防队外，还有距五金店约9公里的司马浦消防救援站派车支援。 当时，吴先生未逃出来的三个孩子躲在房子后侧三楼的防盗窗处，等待救援。 在五金店后门协助救火的邻居陈辉回忆说，当时楼下聚着近二十个街坊，还有人关心三个孩子的安危，用手电筒照着。消防员随后到场升起云梯，用工具剪掉窗外的防盗网将小孩救下。陈辉记不清救下三个孩子花了多长时间，“那个时候连颤抖和害怕的时间都没有，只是帮忙了”。 澎湃新闻记者在现场向陈辉核实，房子三楼处有破拆痕迹的防盗网，即3个小孩逃生处。房子其余各层窗户均有防盗网，部分设置了逃生口，但未打开。尚不清楚逃生口是否上锁，以及遇难者生前是否曾尝试打开。 吴先生回忆说，3个小孩获救后，他以为其他人都跑向了天台。楼内有两个楼梯，分别在楼中间（连接正门）与楼的一侧，均可直通天台，“没有隔断的，只需要一分钟，甚至三十秒都能上去”。而上到天台后有三扇门，“两个没锁，可以直接打开”。 最终，吴先生等来了最为痛心的结果。他得知，除他与妻儿一家八口幸存，其余12位亲人躲在厕所或房间内，全部遇难，包括他的奶奶、父母和两个弟弟及其家人。事后他重返楼内，发现火几乎没烧到楼上，“人是被烟呛死的”。他说，见到遗体时，有遇难亲人的眼睛“还睁开（着）”，他试着把他们的眼睛合上。 从起火到明火被扑灭，过去了43分钟。据汕头市潮南区消防大队发布的警情通报，火灾发生的具体时间是12月9日21时20分，接报后，消防部门迅速调派力量赶赴救援，22时03分，现场明火被扑灭。 事发后，澎湃新闻拍客曾进入火灾现场，发现楼上屋内家具完整，几株植物仍然存活，但阳台和室内烟熏痕迹明显。 高层自建房火灾，浓烟可能是导致死亡的重要原因之一。中国消防科普委员会专家委员刘祖河接受中国新闻周刊采访时说，一旦楼下起火，高温、浓烟和有毒气体沿楼梯急速上蹿，迅速吞噬逃生通道，留给楼上居民的反应时间和逃生空间都极为有限。 据微信公号“广东消防”文章，今年6月14日凌晨，汕头一四层自建房突发大火

(WPVI) -- A fire early Wednesday forced several hundred residents from the Brighton Towers condominiums in Atlantic City, New Jersey, leaving nine units unlivable and sending one police officer to the hospital with minor injuries, according to building management and city officials. The fire appeared to have started in a bedroom on the building's eighth floor. While most residents were allowed back inside after crews brought the incident under control, those living in several corner units remained displaced. The evacuation began around 5 a.m., when residents were jolted awake by pounding on their doors. "Grab your coats and just leave. Or just grab whatever and just leave," resident Deep Halvawala said. "We didn't even have a minute to do anything." Another resident, Perry Lippowitsch, said false alarms were common in the building - but this time the danger was real. "It was pretty scary. Somebody banging on your door. Fire alarms go off a lot. It's usually a false alarm. This time it wasn't," he said. Lippowitsch said he rushed to reach his elderly mother in her unit. "Grabbed the shirt on my back. Went to get out of there. I got my 93-year-old mom, made sure she got out. At least we're all safe," he said. Fire officials said several residents with mobility challenges required assistance evacuating. "We took them out on balconies, covered them in blankets. We kept a firefighter with them," Acting Chief Paul Hess said. "We said we're going back. We had to be able to get them down an evacuation stairwell." Five residents were evaluated on scene and did not need medical treatment, according to city officials. Atlantic City Fire Chief Scott Evans said crews are well acquainted with the property. The high-rise, built in 1966, was the site of a deadly fire in 1969 that killed four people. Evans said the department continues to respond to frequent calls at the building. 标题: E - bike battery caused blaze that sent 2 people to hospital : Edmonton firefigh
正文2000: A blaze that broke out this week at an Edmonton highrise forcing dozens from their homes was caused by a lithium ion battery from an electric bike, officials said as they warned of an increase in these kinds of fires. Assistant Deputy Chief Justin Lallemand of Edmonton Fire Rescue Services said the apartment fire happened Wednesday evening from an electric bike stored on a sixth-floor balcony. Lallemand said two people were sent to hospital and 80 people were evacuated from the building. He added that 20 people have not been able to return to their units. “Over the last few years, as lithium ion batteries become more of a common part of our day, we have seen an increase in fires with these batteries as the cause,” Lallemand said at a news conference Friday. He said firefighters investigated eight fires linked to lithium-ion batteries last year. Lallemand said people should dispose of lithium ion batteries at the city’s eco stations or retailers with the appropriate recycling programs. He also advised people to use the correct batteries and their specific chargers provided or recommended by the manufacturer. “Do not charge devices any longer than necessary and ensure that you are not charging them near any exits you would use to evacuate your home,” he said. “Do not alter or modify the batteries they are using to power micro-mobility devices, power tools, or other battery-operated devices around your home.” Video on social media of the apartment blaze on Wednesday shows fire engulfing the balcony, with flames and smoke shooting out. 正文2000: A gas explosion sent fire racing through the top floors of a high-rise apartment building in New York City early Saturday, killing one person and injuring 14 others as temperatures plunged into the single digits overnight, authorities said. Firefighters responded shortly before 12:30 a.m. to the 17-story building in the Bronx, where people were seen leaning out of windows calling for help as flames engulfed parts of the top floors, officials said. Chief of Department John Esposito said firefighters were investigating reports of a gas odor on the 15th and 16th floors when the explosion occurred. He said there was major structural damage to about a dozen apartments and fires in 10 apartments on the 16th and 17th floors. Authorities did not immediately release information on the person who died. Another person was critically injured, five had serious injuries and eight had minor injuries, officials said. Officials said the building had been undergoing renovations, and work on the natural gas system had been completed and inspected. The cause of the explosion was under investigation. The building was formerly run by the New York City Housing Authority, but it has been under private management since 2024, city officials said. “It’s an incredible tragedy. We’re sending all our thoughts to the families involved,” Leila Bozorg, deputy mayor for housing and planning, said at a morning news conference. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said all utilities in the building were shut down, and all 148 apartments vacated. 标题: Fire erupts inside apartment complex in Hollywood Beach - WSVN 7News | Miami New
正文2000: HOLLYWOOD, FLA. (WSVN) - A fire caused extensive damage to an apartment unit before crews were able to get the upper hand on it. Hollywood Fire Rescue units responded to reports of a fire at an apartment building in the area of New York Street and Hollywood Boulevard, near Hollywood Beach, Tuesday evening. “We have a multi-residential structure with black smoke visible coming from the roof,” said a dispatcher. Flames could be seen shooting out of the windows and balcony of one of the building’s top floor units. Broken glass from the apartment’s window was captured scattered across the sidewalk directly below the unit. Witness John Stinson told 7News he was sitting on the nearby broadwalk with the man who lives inside the unit that caught fire. “He had moved to the north side on the top floor, so I went to go look up to see his apartment, and it was full of smoke coming out of the sliding glass doors,” said Stinson. “He jumped up, immediately ran in. He’s distraught.” The apparent resident of that unit was seen speaking with people outside of the building. “There was so much smoke in the hallway, I dropped my phone, I couldn’t see, I dropped my phone in the hallway, along with the keys, so I couldn’t open the door because there was so much smoke inhalation,” the resident told the crowd. 标题: Residents return to ravaged homes months after Hong Kong fire
正文2000: The city’s deadliest fire in decades killed 168 people when it ripped through seven of the eight apartment blocks at the Wang Fuk Court high-rise complex in November. For the first time since then, around 6,000 residents will be given three-hour windows to enter their homes from Monday and get their belongings. With 1,700 flats to pick through, authorities hope the process will be completed by early May. Officials have advised residents to prepare mentally, with the fire department warning that more than 920 homes had been damaged and some completely destroyed by the blaze. Images released by government officials show the ceilings and walls of some flats have collapsed or been charred black, and the interiors littered with debris. Damaged areas of the residential complex in Hong Kong’s Tai Po district have been cordoned off as “danger zones”, while reinforcement works have been carried where the building structure was compromised. ‘Wouldn’t want to leave’ Survivor Harry Leung, one of the last residents to leave the complex on the day of the blaze, told AFP that he had mixed emotions about his return. While keen to see the flat where he had spent most of his life, he said he was disappointed by the short time frame he was allowed to spend there. Three hours, he said, was not enough time. Hong Kong officials have offered to buy the apartments back around the pre-fire market price, despite the damage, but said that rebuilding the complex on the same site was “not feasible”. “I believe there are actually quite a few people who don’t want to accept (the government’s offer), but have no other options. They’ve been forced to accept it,” Leung told AFP. “If I had a choice, I really wouldn’t want to leave (Wang Fuk Court),” he said. Betty Ho, who plans to return in May to the flat she lived in for more than 30 years, told AFP that what she wants most to retrieve are the photo albums of her childhood. Her family’s “entire life’s possessions are inside that building”, Ho said.

Vehicles unloaded corpses at a mortuary in nearby Sha Tin, another reporter saw, with families expected to arrive in the afternoon for identification. 正文2000: BELMONT, Bronx (WABC) -- Two people were killed and nearly a dozen others were injured during a fire in the Bronx on Tuesday afternoon. It happened on East 187th Street between Belmont and Cambreleng avenues around 1:30 p.m. First responders were met with heavy fire on the first floor, which rapidly raced up the stairs, spreading to all floors of the five-story building. The building is home to a barbershop and deli on the ground floor as well as six apartment units on floors two through five. FDNY officials say firefighters extinguished fire on the first floor fours, but when they hit the top floor, the roof collapsed throughout a large portion of the building, as did part of the stairwell. Firefighters then moved to exterior operations, and rescued several people in the back and front of the building, including a civilian who had to be rescued by firefighters from a window via a ladder. Several others were rescued from a fire escape. "56 truck rescued a civilian trapped in a window with no access to a fire escape and rescued that victim via portable ladder," said FDNY Chief of Operations Kevin Woods. 正文2000: Commentary The Hong Kong high-rise fire shows how difficult it is to evacuate in an emergency Human behaviour is one of the biggest sources of delay in high-rise evacuations. Milad Haghani, Erica Kuligowski and Ruggiero Lovreglio The Hong Kong high-rise fire, which spread across multiple buildings in a large residential complex, has killed dozens, with hundreds reported missing. The death toll at the time of writing was over 40, with close to 300 people still unaccounted for and dozens in hospital with serious injuries. This makes it one of Hong Kong’s deadliest building fires in living memory, and already the worst since the Garley Building fire in 1996. The stakes are highest in the buildings that are full at predictable times: residential towers at night, office towers in the day. We’ve seen this in the biggest modern examples, from the World Trade Center in the United States to Grenfell Tower in the United Kingdom. The patterns repeat: once a fire takes hold, getting thousands of people safely down dozens of storeys becomes a race against time. 正文2000: “火（烧得）特别快，‘呼’就起来了，风一吹，就往楼上冲，烧得‘砰砰’响。” 香港新界大埔屋邨宏福苑多栋住宅楼发生火灾，已造成至少44人遇难，45人受伤。一夜过后，已看不到大面积明火，但火势尚未完全扑灭。 今晨7时30分许，肖南笙看到宏福苑的火仍未熄灭（图/新京报） 视频显示，火势在多栋居民楼迅速蔓延。火灾发生时，建于1983年的宏福苑的居民楼正经历维修。据新华社消息，香港警方展开调查，发现着火建筑物外墙有保护网、防水帆布、塑料布，疑未符合防火标准，另有一座未波及的大厦每层电梯大堂窗外都有发泡胶包封，易燃且可能加速火势蔓延，不排除发泡胶是火势迅速蔓延的原因。 正文2000: “宏业建筑”是此次宏福苑装修的承建商，这家公司曾涉嫌贿赂贪污、参与围标、施工安全等多次违规事件（图/视觉中国） 文｜《财经》研究员 黄思韵 编辑｜刘以秦 2025年11月26日，香港大埔宏福苑发生五级火灾，七座大厦失火。火势连烧超过30个小时，截至今日（28日）早上6时，火灾累计造成94人死亡，仍有200多人失踪。 11月27日晚上10点，《财经》在火灾现场看到，高层还有明火，不断有带火星的碎片掉落。距离宏福苑不到1公里的周边，烟味弥漫，救护车的鸣笛声时远时近。周边道路封闭，路边和车库都有预备消防车和救护车，一波波的市民带着物资箱来到现场发放。 她尝试致电管理处求证，但打了两三次电话，都打不通。打开电视后，看到新闻正在播报“宏福苑三级火”。火警报警器在下午3点多响了起来，她开门撞见邻居，邻居也搞不清状况，先一步下楼看看局势，后赶紧打电话让赵姨离开。 下午3点45分，赵姨攥着手机，背上小包，看到电梯正常运行，松了一口气。还坐了电梯，电梯只有她一个人。原本以为火势没有那么严重，盘算着如果问题不大再回屋收拾东西。但一出楼栋，两三个警员朝她大喊，“快点走，危险”。她想回头望一眼着火方向，被要求快速撤离，怕有燃烧的碎片剥落。 15分钟后，赵姨看到隔壁楼火势蔓延到自己楼栋，“就是一瞬间的事”。 （27日上午，赵姨家楼下的火灾情况，拍摄/黄思韵） 受风向影响，3座是8座楼栋中火势较大的楼栋之一。11月27日晚上，火势受到控制，2座和4座楼栋残留绿色围网，3座外墙几乎全黑。去往亲戚家借住的路上，赵姨和同楼栋高楼层的邻居交流，大家互相安慰，平安就好。 “现在（3栋）就像废墟。”邻居苦笑。“屋企乜都冇曬，烧到通晒窿（家什么都没了，烧成窟窿）”，赵姨说。 标题: FDNY says closing doors could have avoided deaths in 5 - alarm Bronx fire
正文2000: A five-alarm Bronx fire that killed two people on Tuesday afternoon spread quickly because multiple doors were left open, according to the FDNY. FDNY officials said firefighters arrived just minutes after the flames broke out at the five-story apartment building on East 187th Street in Belmont. They found heavy smoke and fire on all floors of the building, according to officials. The FDNY said an ongoing investigation found multiple doors in the building were left open, including the one to the apartment where fire marshals believe the fire started. “Door was left open to the fire apartment, door was left open to the front of the building, and the door was left open to the bulkhead, which is the exit to the roof,” FDNY First Deputy Commissioner Daniel Flynn said at a press briefing Friday morning. “If not for those doors being open, we believe that the fire may have even been contained in that one apartment, and we would have not, not had lost anybody.” Officials also said people in the Bronx building did not use the building’s fire escapes, and that the building’s door was propped open. On Thursday, they urged New Yorkers to ensure they always close the door behind them in the event of a fire, and also ensure their windows are not blocked and that they can access their fire escapes. “ Walk out onto the fire escape, show your children where the fire escapes are. Do not get caught off guard when these fires occur,” Flynn said. “Always know how you're going to escape.” Flynn said the two victims of Tuesday’s fire were found in the stairwell, and said they were making their way down from higher floors. It’s been an active week for the FDNY. On Thursday, firefighters responded to a five-alarm fire at a church in Queens. It does take more time, but we also send a lot more crews, staff, firefighters to the scene,” he said. “We have systems in place for calls like this.” The investigation into the cause, origin, and circumstances of this fire, which is a joint effort between Toronto police, the Ontario Fire Marshal’s office and our own TFS investigators, is in the early stages, Hewson said.

标题: 刻不容缓 ！ 一场与时间赛跑的紧急救援 -- 中国警察网
正文2000: 10月23日凌晨，按照安徽省马鞍山市公安局花山分局常态化夜间巡防部署，绿地警务站民警潘小虎与辅警张文龙沿朝霞路开展巡逻值守。行至某居民小区附近时，潘小虎凭借多年夜巡积累的敏锐洞察力，发现临街一栋高层住宅楼20多层处有异常火光闪烁。 因高层建筑遮挡，无法锁定起火楼层，二人当即分工：潘小虎前往小区，同步向上级详细汇报火情位置、现场火势等实时动态；张文龙紧随其后，在小区入口做好秩序维护与引导准备。 “不确定火源，就从20层开始逐层排查！”面对紧急态势，二人迅速敲定方案，沿楼梯从20层开始逐层向上排查。随着排查推进，空气中的焦糊味愈发浓烈。当二人排查至25层时，一股刺鼻浓烟从一户居民家门缝渗出，起火点找到了！ 潘小虎一边向指挥中心上报起火点准确地址，请求支援警力及消防力量紧急驰援，一边与张文龙轮番用力敲打起火住户房门。“屋里有人吗？着火了，快开门！”急促的呼叫声与敲门声在空旷的楼道内回荡，屋内却始终无人回应。 因房门为加固结构，二人尝试撬动、撞击均无法打开。情况愈发紧急，潘小虎继续在门外呼喊提醒，张文龙则迅速逐户敲门，引导25层及以上住户有序向楼下安全区域疏散。 随后，花山分局特巡警大队、霍里派出所警力接到指挥中心支援指令后迅速响应，火速抵达现场，共同疏导住户30余人，并同步引导消防救援车、120急救车顺利入场。很快，消防救援力量与120急救人员相继赶到。 消防救援人员使用破拆工具打开起火房门，浓烟与热浪瞬间涌出。消防救援人员迅速展开灭火救援，仅用10分钟便成功控制住火势，并救出被困在卧室内的谷先生一家四口，其中包括一名年仅1岁的幼儿。经120急救人员初步检查，4人虽吸入少量浓烟，但意识清醒，随后被紧急送往医院做进一步观察。 “当晚家中用电饭锅炖煮排骨后忘记关闭电源，全家睡着后未察觉异常，连门外的救援呼喊和敲门声都没听见。”事后，谷先生回忆事发经过时仍心有余悸。参与救援的消防救援人员表示，凌晨时段是居民熟睡、安全防范意识最薄弱的时期，若火情未被及时发现，待火势与浓烟大范围蔓延后，极可能造成无法挽回的后果。睡前要仔细检查相关电器、煤气灶是否关闭。 据悉，花山分局科学规划16条夜间警力必巡路线，在重点商圈、居民小区、交通要道设置12个必守点位，通过“定点值守+动态巡逻”的常态化模式，全力守护群众安全。 “花山分局通过夜间巡防工作筑牢辖区治安防线，全力守护群众生命财产安全。”花山分局副局长张阅表示。据统计，今年以来，该局通过夜间巡防累计及时发现并处置各类安全隐患146起，协助侦破案件149起，为群众办实事、解难题890余次。
